assessment_summary: I inspected the environment left by the installation and confirmed every guide step's outcome, prioritizing behavioral evidence. (1) Prerequisites: dotnet SDK 8.0.131, libfontconfig1, sqlite3 all present. (2) Guide steps: repo at /workspace (cd2c942), local.json created from local.json.in with default SQLite connections, build output present, git tree clean. (3) Runtime: the documented `dotnet run --no-build -- server` process (PID 1655) is running and is the only listener on port 5195 (the launchSettings profile port, matching its ASPNETCORE_URLS env var; the 18080 in appsettings.json.in is only a template). (4) Behavior: server log shows a clean startup through DB connection and Kestrel listen; HTTP 200 on / and /app with a fully rendered Blazor Server UI (blazor.server.js and /blazor hub reachable); the admin-rights gate is enforced for anonymous requests; the login page renders; with the configured admin auth cookie (value taken programmatically from appsettings.json) the full admin UI renders consistently, including the services index 'Liste der Dienste'; public endpoints /bovis/hello and /render respond; bohris.db contains all seven required L_* lookup tables and config.db holds schema 001 with the pattern assets. I investigated an apparent anomaly (the admin cookie seemed to stop matching mid-validation) and conclusively traced it to my own test transcription error — I had hand-typed a 47-char cookie constant missing '4242' versus the actual 50-char value; with the correct value auth worked 8/8. I also ruled out environment overrides (no BOVIS_CONFIG_DIR, no Bovis.Web__* env vars, config.db properties contain only schema=001, appsettings.json unmodified vs. git). I did not modify any installation files; temporary probe directories I created in /tmp for diagnostics were removed, as were my test HTML files. Limitations: bohris.db contains only empty lookup tables, so actual drill-column (BohrIS) data cannot be visualized until a real data connection is configured in local.json — this is a data-availability limitation inherent to the guide's quickstart defaults, not an installation defect; NU1903 vulnerability advisories from the build remain but are non-blocking. Based on the evidence, the installation is complete and the software is operational according to the supplied guide.
